verses.zh: 以萨迦的儿子是陀拉、普瓦、雅述（在创世记四十六章十三节是约伯）、伸仑，共四人。
verses.en: The sons of Issachar: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron—four in all.

verses.zh: 陀拉的儿子是乌西、利法雅、耶勒、雅买、易伯散、示母利，都是陀拉的族长，是大能的勇士。到大卫年间，他们的人数共有二万二千六百名。
verses.en: The sons of Tola: Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam,[NOTE:1] and Samuel.[NOTE:2] They were leaders of their families.[NOTE:3] In the time of David there were 22,600 warriors listed in Tola’s genealogical records.[NOTE:4]
notes: Many English versions spell this name “Ibsam.”
Many English versions retain a form of this name closer to the Hebrew, i.e., “Shemuel.”
Heb “heads of the house of their fathers.”
Heb “to Tola [there were] warriors by their generations, their number in the days of David [was] 22,600.”
verses.commentary:
7:2 "mighty men of valor" This phrase, referring to their fighting ability and bravery, is also mentioned in
1 Chr. 7:5,7,9,11,40.

▣ "in the days of David" Therefore, the above phrase refers to "the mighty men" of David's day, whether
before he was king or after is not stated, but usually refers to before.

▣ "22,600" There are many numbers in this chapter that do not agree with the book of Numbers. A good
resource to understand some of the number problems in the OT is G. E. Mendenhall, The Census Lists of Numbers 1
and 26, JBL 77 (1958), pp. 52-66.

verses.zh: 乌西的儿子是伊斯拉希；伊斯拉希的儿子是米迦勒、俄巴底亚、约珥、伊示雅，共五人，都是族长。
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Uzzi: Izrahiah.The sons of Izrahiah: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Isshiah. All five were leaders.
notes: The Hebrew text has the plural “sons,” but only one son is listed.
verses.commentary:
7:3 "all five of them were chief men" This shows the selective nature of these genealogies or that the word
"chief" (BDB 910) had a different meaning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HEAD

verses.zh: 他们所率领的，按着宗族出战的军队，共有三万六千人，因为他们的妻和子众多。
verses.en: According to the genealogical records of their families, they had 36,000 warriors available for battle, for they had numerous wives and sons.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and unto them by their generations to the house of their fathers [were] troops of war of battle, 36,000, for they had many wives and sons.”
verses.commentary:
7:4

NASB, NKJV, NJB
"troops"

NRSV, JPSOA
"units"

REB, NASB margin
"bands"

LXX
"strong ones"

Peshitta
"valiant men of war"

The MT has "band" or "troop" (BDB 151, cf. 2 Chr. 25:9,10; 26:11). The army was divided into
fighting units. This issue is complicated by a similar use of the word "thousand" for a military unit.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THOUSAND (eleph)

verses.zh: 他们的族弟兄在以萨迦各族中都是大能的勇士，按着家谱计算共有八万七千人。
verses.en: Altogether the genealogical records of the clans of Issachar listed 87,000 warriors.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and their brothers, according to all the clans of Issachar, the warriors [were] 87,000 listed in the genealogical records for all.”

verses.zh: 便雅悯的儿子是比拉、比结、耶叠，共三人。
verses.en: The sons of Benjamin:[NOTE:1] Bela, Beker, and Jediael—three in all.
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “Benjamin,” but בְּנֵי (bene, “sons of”) has dropped out by haplography (בְּנֵי בִּנְיָמִן, bene binyamin).
verses.commentary:
7:6-12 It is uncertain why Benjamin is mentioned in this list of northern genealogies. The list of Bela's
descendants is expanded in 1 Chronicles 8, especially the person of Ehud (2 Chr. 8:6). He is one of the Judges
(cf. Judges 3) who killed the king of Moab, Eglon, and delivered Israel.

verses.zh: 比拉的儿子是以斯本、乌西、乌薛、耶利摩、以利，共五人，都是族长，是大能的勇士。按着家谱计算，他们的子孙共有二万二千零三十四人。
verses.en: The sons of Bela: Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri. The five of them were leaders of their families. There were 22,034 warriors listed in their genealogical records.

verses.zh: 比结的儿子是细米拉、约阿施、以利以谢、以利约乃、暗利、耶利摩、亚比雅、亚拿突、亚拉篾。这都是比结的儿子。
verses.en: The sons of Beker: Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jeremoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth. All these were the sons of Beker.

verses.zh: 他们都是族长，是大能的勇士。按着家谱计算，他们的子孙共有二万零二百人。
verses.en: There were 20,200 family leaders and warriors listed in their genealogical records.

verses.zh: 耶叠的儿子是比勒罕；比勒罕的儿子是耶乌施、便雅悯、以忽、基拿拿、细坦、他施、亚希沙哈。
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Jediael: Bilhan.The sons of Bilhan: Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Kenaanah, Zethan, Tarshish, and Ahishahar.
notes: The Hebrew text has the plural “sons,” but only one son is listed.
verses.commentary:
7:10 "Jeush" The Kethiv (MT) is "Jeish," but the Qere (Masoretic scholars' suggestion)
is "Jeush."

verses.zh: 这都是耶叠的儿子，都是族长，是大能的勇士；他们的子孙能上阵打仗的，共有一万七千二百人。
verses.en: All these were the sons of Jediael. There were 17,200 family leaders and warriors who were capable of marching out to battle.

verses.zh: 还有以珥的儿子书品、户品，并亚黑的儿子户伸。
verses.en: The Shuppites and Huppites were descendants of Ir; the Hushites were descendants of Aher.[NOTE:1]
notes: The name “Aher” appears as “Ahiram” in Num 26:38.
verses.commentary:
7:12 "Shuppim" In Gen. 46:21, "Muppim." Because they are PLURAL, these names may
reflect clans not an individual (cf. 1 Chr. 7:15).

▣ "Huppim" In Numbers 26:39 it is "Hupham."

▣ "Ir" In 1 Chr. 7:7, "Iri."

▣ "Hushim" In both the genealogies of Israel in Genesis 46 and Numbers 26, the list of Dan's descendants
follows the list of Benjamin's descendants. Surprisingly, Dan is omitted here. But because the name "Hushim" does not appear,
which is the name of both a Benjamite (here) and a Danite (cf. Gen. 46:23), some have suggested parts of the original genealogy
have dropped out of the text.

SPECIAL TOPIC: TEXTUAL CRITICISM

▣ "Aher" In Numbers 26:38, "Ahiram."

verses.zh: 拿弗他利的儿子是雅薛、沽尼、耶色、沙龙。这都是辟拉的子孙。
verses.en: The sons of Naphtali: Jahziel,[NOTE:1] Guni, Jezer, and Shallum[NOTE:2]—sons of Bilhah.
notes: Most Hebrew mss read “Shallum”; some Hebrew mss and some LXX mss read “Shillem,” the form of the name that appears in Gen 46:24 and Num 26:49.
See the note on the word “concubine” in 1:32.
verses.commentary:
7:13 The brevity of the list of Naphtali is purposeful or records have been lost. This list follows Gen. 46:24-25.

▣ "Jahziel" In Gen. 46:24, "Jahzeel."

▣ "Shallum" In Gen. 46:24 and Num. 26:49, "Shillem."

▣ "the sons of Bilhah" She bore to Jacob "Dan" and "Naphtali" (cf. Gen. 46:23-25).

verses.zh: 玛拿西的儿子亚斯列是他妾亚兰人所生的，又生了基列之父玛吉。
verses.en: The sons of Manasseh: Asriel, who was born to Manasseh’s Aramean concubine.[NOTE:1] She also gave birth to Makir the father of Gilead.
notes: Some translations treat the terms שֻׁפִּים (shuppim) and חֻפִּים (khuppim) as proper names of individuals (“Huppim” and “Shuppim”), but others consider these forms to be plurals and refer to tribal or clan names.
verses.commentary:
7:14-19 This paragraph mentions women an unusual number of times.

- 1 Chr. 7:14, "his Aramean concubine"

- 1 Chr. 7:15, "a wife. . .whose sister's name was Maacah"

- 1 Chr. 7:15, "daughters"

- 1 Chr. 7:16, "she named him"

- 1 Chr. 7:18, "his sister"

This listing is meant to represent the part of Manasseh that settled in Canaan.

verses.zh: 玛吉娶的妻是户品、书品的妹子，名叫玛迦。玛拿西的次子名叫西罗非哈；西罗非哈但有几个女儿。
verses.en: Now Makir married a wife from the Huppites and Shuppites.[NOTE:1] (His sister’s name was Maacah.)Zelophehad was Manasseh’s second son;[NOTE:2] he had only daughters.
notes: Heb “and the name of the second was Zelophehad.”
The Hebrew text has the plural “sons,” but only one son is listed.
verses.commentary:
7:15 "Huppim and Shuppim" Because these are PLURAL, some scholars think they might be clans.

▣ "Maacah" The LXX has "Moocha" and places it in verse 16.

▣ "Zelophehad had daughters" This is also recorded in Num. 26:33. In Numbers 27 these daughters ask
Moses to allow them to inherit their father's land because all the male children died, and Moses does, so as to keep the
God-given land (cf. Joshua) in the tribe and family.

verses.zh: 玛吉的妻玛迦生了一个儿子，起名叫毗利施。毗利施的兄弟名叫示利施；示利施的儿子是乌兰和利金。
verses.en: Maacah, Makir’s wife, gave birth to a son, whom she named Peresh. His brother was Sheresh, and his sons were Ulam and Rekem.

verses.zh: 乌兰的儿子是比但。这都是基列的子孙。基列是玛吉的儿子，玛吉是玛拿西的儿子。
verses.en: The son[NOTE:1] of Ulam: Bedan. These were the sons of Gilead, son of Makir, son of Manasseh.
notes: The expression בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel) means “come to” or “approach,” but is also used as a euphemism for sexual relations.

verses.zh: 基列的妹子哈摩利吉生了伊施荷、亚比以谢、玛拉。
verses.en: His sister Hammoleketh gave birth to Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

verses.zh: 〈示米大的儿子是亚现、示剑、利克希、阿尼安。〉
verses.en: The sons of Shemida were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

verses.zh: 以法莲的儿子是书提拉；书提拉的儿子是比列；比列的儿子是他哈；他哈的儿子是以拉大；以拉大的儿子是他哈；
verses.en: The descendants of Ephraim: Shuthelah, his son Bered, his son Tahath, his son Eleadah, his son Tahath,

verses.zh: 他哈的儿子是撒拔；撒拔的儿子是书提拉。以法莲又生以谢、以列；这二人因为下去夺取迦特人的牲畜，被本地的迦特人杀了。
verses.en: his son Zabad, his son Shuthelah (Ezer and Elead were killed by the men of Gath, who were natives of the land, when they went down to steal their cattle.
verses.commentary:
7:21-23 This is a brief historical note explaining the name "Beriah" (a PREPOSITION,
ב plus root BDB 947 = the name, BDB 140), which means "trouble" or "tragedy"
(BDB 947).

verses.zh: 他们的父亲以法莲为他们悲哀了多日，他的弟兄都来安慰他。
verses.en: Their father Ephraim mourned for them many days and his brothers came to console him.

verses.zh: 以法莲与妻同房，他妻就怀孕生了一子，以法莲因为家里遭祸，就给这儿子起名叫比利亚。
verses.en: He slept with[NOTE:1] his wife; she became pregnant and gave birth to a son. Ephraim[NOTE:2] named him Beriah because tragedy had come to his family.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ephraim) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “because in tragedy there had come to his house.” The preposition prefixed to רָעָה (raʿah) should probably be omitted. The Hebrew noun רָעָה (“tragedy”) should be understood as the subject of the feminine verb form that follows.
The antecedent of the pronoun “his” is not clear. The translation assumes that v. 25 resumes the list of Ephraim’s descendants (see vv. 20-21a) after a lengthy parenthesis (vv. 21b-24).

verses.zh: 他的女儿名叫舍伊拉，就是建筑上伯・和仑、下伯・和仑与乌羡・舍伊拉的。
verses.en: His daughter was Sheerah, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, as well as Uzzen Sheerah),
verses.commentary:
7:24 This is another brief historical note about the building projects of Ephraim's granddaughter, "Sheerah."

"Beth-horon" was a levitical city in the tribal allocation of Ephraim.

"Uzzen-sheerah," a city name, occurs only here in the OT. Sheerah built three cities.

verses.zh: 比利亚的儿子是利法和利悉。利悉的儿子是他拉；他拉的儿子是他罕；
verses.en: his[NOTE:1] son Rephah, his son Resheph,[NOTE:2] his son Telah, his son Tahan,
notes: The Hebrew text has simply “Resheph,” but the phrase “his son” has probably been accidentally omitted, since the names before and after this one include the phrase.
Heb “Non” (so KJV, NASB; cf. Exod 33:11, where the more familiar spelling “Nun” occurs).

verses.zh: 他罕的儿子是拉但；拉但的儿子是亚米忽；亚米忽的儿子是以利沙玛；
verses.en: his son Ladan, his son Ammihud, his son Elishama,

verses.zh: 以利沙玛的儿子是嫩；嫩的儿子是约书亚。
verses.en: his son Nun,[NOTE:1] and his son Joshua.
notes: For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
verses.commentary: 7:27 "Non" In Exod. 33:11 "Nun." This is the father of Joshua, the servant and later successor of Moses.

verses.zh: 以法莲人的地业和住处是伯特利与其村庄；东边拿兰，西边基色与其村庄；示剑与其村庄，直到迦萨与其村庄；
verses.en: Their property and settlements included Bethel[NOTE:1] and its surrounding towns, Naaran to the east, Gezer and its surrounding towns to the west, and Shechem and its surrounding towns as far as Ayyah and its surrounding towns.
notes: “Beth Shean” is a variant spelling of “Beth Shan.”
verses.commentary:
7:28 "Naaran" In Joshua 16:7, "Naarah."

▣ "Ayyah" In LXX, Targums, Vulgate, "Azzah" or "Gazza" (NEB). The UBS Text Project (p. 407) gives
"Ayyah" a "B" rating (some doubt).

▣ "with its towns" This phrase refers to the unwalled villages surrounding larger cities.

verses.zh: 还有靠近玛拿西人的境界，伯・善与其村庄；他纳与其村庄；米吉多与其村庄；多珥与其村庄。以色列儿子约瑟的子孙住在这些地方。
verses.en: On the border of Manasseh’s territory were Beth Shean[NOTE:1] and its surrounding towns, Taanach and its surrounding towns, Megiddo[NOTE:2] and its surrounding towns, and Dor and its surrounding towns. The descendants of Joseph, Israel’s son, lived here.
notes: For location see Map1-D4; Map2-C1; Map4-C2; Map5-F2; Map7-B1.

The Hebrew text has אֲחִי (ʾakhi, “the brother of”), but this should probably be emended to אֲחִיו (ʾakhiv, “his brother”). Cf. v. 35. Most English versions treat this Hebrew word as a proper name (“Ahi”) and list it before “Rohgah.”
verses.commentary:
7:29 "Beth-shean" This (cf. Jos. 17:11,16; Jdgs. 1:27) is a variant spelling of "Beth-shan," a city in the
tribal allocation of Manasseh (cf. 1 Sam. 31:10,12).

verses.zh: 亚设的儿子是音拿、亦施瓦、亦施韦、比利亚，还有他们的妹子西拉。
verses.en: The sons of Asher: Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Serah was their sister.

verses.zh: 比利亚的儿子是希别、玛结；玛结是比撒威的父亲。
verses.en: The sons of Beriah: Heber and Malkiel, who was the father of Birzaith.

verses.zh: 希别生雅弗勒、朔默、何坦，和他们的妹子书雅。
verses.en: Heber was the father of Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and Shua their sister.
verses.commentary:
7:32 "Shomer" In 1 Chr. 7:34 the same person's name is spelled "Shemer."

▣ "Hotham" In 1 Chr. 7:35 the name is spelled "Helen."

verses.zh: 雅弗勒的儿子是巴萨、宾哈、亚施法。这都是雅弗勒的儿子。
verses.en: The sons of Japhlet: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath. These were Japhlet’s sons.

verses.zh: 朔默的儿子是亚希、罗迦、耶户巴、亚兰。
verses.en: The sons of his brother[NOTE:1] Shemer:[NOTE:2] Rohgah, Hubbah,[NOTE:3] and Aram.
notes: Or “Shomer,” cf. v. 32.
“Hubbah” is the marginal reading (Qere); the consonantal text (Kethib) has “Jachbah.”
Or “Hotham,” cf. v. 32.
verses.commentary: 7:34 "were Ahi" It is possible that the MT should read "his brother" (BDB 26, TEV, NJB).

verses.zh: 朔默兄弟希连的儿子是琐法、音那、示利斯、亚抹。
verses.en: The sons of his brother Helem:[NOTE:1] Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.
notes: The name “Ithran” is sometimes understood to be another name for “Jether” (v. 38).

verses.zh: 琐法的儿子是书亚、哈尼弗、书阿勒、比利、音拉、
verses.en: The sons of Zophah: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, Imrah,

verses.zh: 比悉、河得、珊玛、施沙、益兰、比拉。
verses.en: Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Ithran,[NOTE:1] and Beera.
notes: Heb “all these were the sons of Asher, heads of the house of the fathers, selected, warriors, heads of the leaders, and there was listed in the genealogical records in war, in battle, their number, men, 26,000.”

verses.zh: 益帖的儿子是耶孚尼、毗斯巴、亚拉。
verses.en: The sons of Jether: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.

verses.zh: 乌拉的儿子是亚拉、汉尼业、利写。
verses.en: The sons of Ulla: Arah, Hanniel, and Rizia.

verses.zh: 这都是亚设的子孙，都是族长，是精壮大能的勇士，也是首领中的头目，按着家谱计算，他们的子孙能出战的共有二万六千人。
verses.en: All these were the descendants of Asher. They were the leaders of their families, the most capable men, who were warriors and served as head chiefs. There were 26,000 warriors listed in their genealogical records as capable of doing battle.[NOTE:1]
verses.commentary:
7:40 Notice how the sons of Asher are characterized.

- choice

- mighty men of valor

- heads of the princes

These were important military people/leaders.

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT THE PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects. Compare your subject divisions with the five translations
above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation.
Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

- Second paragraph

- Etc.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- This is a brief genealogy of the northern tribes.

- Issachar ‒ 1 Chr. 7:1-5

- Benjamin (poss. Dan) ‒ 1 Chr. 7:6-12

- Naphtali ‒ 1 Chr. 7:13

- Manasseh ‒ 1 Chr. 7:14-19

- Ephraim ‒ 1 Chr. 7:20-27

- Asher ‒ 1 Chr. 7:30-40

- Why is there such divergence in the spelling of the names?

- They are different persons by the same name. Often names recur in families and periods.

- There are two separate genealogies combined by an editor.

- The person went by two names.

- The person's name was changed.

- The term "son" can refer to a wide number of relatives (grandson, uncle, brother, etc.).

- The first father died and the wife remarried or there was Levirate marriage involved.

- Ancient Jewish genealogies are often incomplete.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 7:1-5

1Now the sons of Issachar were four: Tola, Puah, Jashub and Shimron. 2The sons of
Tola were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Ibsam and Samuel, heads of their fathers' households. The sons
of Tola were mighty men of valor in their generations; their number in the days of David was 22,600. 3The
son of Uzzi was Izrahiah. And the sons of Izrahiah were Michael, Obadiah, Joel, Isshiah; all five of them
were chief men. 4With them by their generations according to their fathers' households were 36,000
troops of the army for war, for they had many wives and sons. 5Their relatives among all the families of Issachar
were mighty men of valor, enrolled by genealogy, in all 87,000.
